_comment: The zero-modification contract, as data. `checked` is the build + CI plumbing: every file upstream ships that this
project promised not to fork, so that the next scaffold release merges without replaying private code.
`sha256` is upstream's pinned bytes; the gate compares the working tree against them.
`tolerated` is the honest list of files that currently *are* forked, each with why and what removes it. It is a
ratchet: the count may not rise, and an entry that has become identical is itself a failure, because a stale
tolerance hides the next real divergence.
Not in this tier, with reasons: `.include-guard.txt` (the scaffold's own docstring says a derived project states its
layering in that file), `.github/skills/**` (agent guidance, project-specific by design), and every content path --
README, metadata.json, include/, src/, api/, benchmark/, docs sources, tests, editor settings.
each one is in a file that an upstream caller names **by path** -- .mega-linter.yml is named by
.github/workflows/security-linters.yml:118 and :138 (MEGALINTER_CONFIG) and by run-megalinter.sh, and
docs/build.py is named by .github/workflows/docs-build.yml:35 -- while all five of those files are themselves in
this same byte-checked tier. Moving the private bits into an environment variable or a wrapper therefore moves the
fork to another checked file instead of removing it. The exits below are upstream patches 0019/0020, verified to
apply on 6d69c85 and to reproduce these files byte for byte. For .mega-linter.yml a private-side alternative does
exist -- splitting the eleven functions that trip cppcheck's analysis limit would let upstream's bytes pass, at
the cost of real code churn -- and for docs/build.py it does not: those 109 lines fix three defects (lost block
closers, swallowed lead text on continuation lines, a selection that outlives its comment), so reverting means
accepting silent loss of published text.
Closed on 2026-11-04 by upstream v0.3.4 (701a2452): `f2519753` and `98ea19a1` took the cppcheck argument for
both the C and the CPP descriptor (more than the 0019 patch asked for), and `88f796b3` took the bilingual
filter fixes. `tolerated` is now empty and `baseline_divergences` is 0; the two proposed patches under
upstream-patches/ are kept as the record of what was asked for, marked merged. The paragraph that used to
argue the forks could not be closed privately was correct only while upstream had not shipped a release --
which is the argument for keeping an exit plan executable rather than a sentence.

declared_additions..license-guard.txt: rule data for this project's licence gate, in the same class as .include-guard.txt, which the scaffold's own cmd_guard docstring says a derived project states itself

.github/misc.why_checked: eight project scripts had collected here (claim/capability/coverage/docfmt/number-sheet/arbiter/assume/anchor) and a byte-check of the files upstream ships cannot see a directory that has grown extras -- which is precisely how the private code got in. The file set is compared, not only the contents.

not_checked.conandata.yml: the project's own dependency list (gtest / etl / pybind11 here). The template's metadata-contract describes this file as the place a project states its requirements, so a different content is the intended state, not a fork.
not_checked..include-guard.txt: the scaffold's cmd_guard docstring says a derived project states its own layering in this file, so editing it is the sanctioned mechanism.
